items.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expected to orchestrate diverse tools over long-horizon tasks. Existing agents typically use Direct Tool Calling (DTC), where the model invokes tools sequentially, and tool responses accumulate in the model context, which can lead to context rot and orchestration breakdown. In contrast, Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) invokes tools through executable code and stores intermediate results in runtime variables rather than appending them to the context. Prior work has explored PTC mainly as an inference-time optimization, but its benefits for agentic training remain unclear, and suitable verifiable training tasks are scarce. In this work, we introduce ProgAgent, a full PTC training stack, comprising a pipeline for synthesizing verifiable long-horizon tasks, a lightweight PTC runtime, and a two-stage training recipe. Using only 215 tasks instantiated at four environment scales, ProgAgent yields higher pass rates than the evaluated baselines of comparable size across four benchmarks. On LOCA-bench, ProgAgent-14B achieves a 30.7% pass rate at a 64k-token environment state, where these baselines score zero. Cross-harness experiments show that PTC-trained models outperform DTC-trained models under both evaluation interfaces, suggesting that the benefits of PTC training extend beyond the interface.

items.title: Proposed Ergonomic Workstation Design Based on REBA to Minimize Musculoskeletal Disorder Risks in the Injection Molding Process
items.abstract: In the injection section of PT Natamas Plast, product sorting activities are performed using workstations with different types and dimensions of chairs and tables that have not been fully adjusted to operator anthropometric characteristics. This condition may result in non-ergonomic working postures and musculoskeletal discomfort. This study aimed to identify ergonomic problems in the product sorting workstation and provide a basis for ergonomic workstation redesign. The study was conducted through direct observation of working conditions and assessment of musculoskeletal complaints using NBM, while working posture was evaluated using REBA. The NBM results showed that operators experienced musculoskeletal complaints, particularly in the lower back, calves, and buttocks with the percentage complaints above 4%. The REBA assessment indicates that 5 out of the 9 operators are classified as having a high-risk level ranging score from 8 to 10. Anthropometric measurements were also performed to determine the workstation dimensions based on the 5th to 95th percentile, resulting in a proposed adjustable chair with a height of 39 to 49 cm and an adjustable worktable height from 136 to 159 cm. The proposed workstation design integrates musculoskeletal complaints, postural risk, and operator anthropometry to improve compatibility between the operator and workstation. The main contribution of this study is the development of a proposed ergonomic workstation based on REBA assessment and operator anthropometric data, which provides a technically justified intervention for mitigating identified ergonomic risks and serves as a basis for future implementation.

items.title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.

items.title: Query-Adaptive Neuron Steering for LLMs
items.abstract: Effectively eliciting the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) at inference time remains an important challenge. Existing studies address this challenge through context engineering, which shapes user queries, or fixed steering, which directly intervenes in model computation. However, predefined contexts and fixed intervention strategies may not adequately accommodate the diverse knowledge and reasoning requirements of individual queries. This raises a natural question: Can internal steering in LLMs be made query-adaptive? In this work, we investigate whether query-induced internal activations can guide adaptive steering in LLMs. Our pilot studies reveal subject- and layer-dependent neuron activation patterns and show that amplifying subject-relevant neurons can improve model performance. Based on these findings, we propose Q-NeuS, a query-adaptive neuron steering framework that dynamically determines which neurons to modulate and by how much for each input. Specifically, Q-NeuS constructs a compact subject-guided candidate neuron space and employs a lightweight Query-Adaptive Gate to generate neuron-wise modulation coefficients. To learn effective intervention strategies, we introduce Neu-GRPO, which adapts group-relative optimization to train the Query-Adaptive Gate using the relative performance of multiple neuron intervention configurations. The base LLM remains frozen throughout training and inference, and no task or subject labels are required at inference time. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that Q-NeuS consistently improves model performance and exhibits broad applicability across model scales and strong cross-benchmark transferability.

items.title: Re-executing Coding-Agent Evaluations: Unchanged Decisions and Unresolved Policy Risk
items.abstract: Executable tests grade large language model (LLM) coding-agent patches for leaderboards, rewards and self-improvement. Two preregistered re-execution studies returned negative results. SWE-bench Pro v1's offline option rejected none of 59 accepted Go patches whose grading configuration changed. Their exploratory, unweighted upper confidence limit is 4.95% under candidate independence, leaving a 3% exposed-patch risk unresolved; the preregistered estimator uses inverse sampling-probability weights. An extension was inconclusive. In a selected stratum, a reconstructed module cache built from the reference solution's dependencies rejected accepted alternatives from four models that passed with their own dependencies. Re-executing 1,929 selected agent-version/task evaluations from the Darwin Gödel Machine's archive preserved best-agent selection and system-variant ranking, with search history and scores of evaluations not rerun fixed. Exploratory host, image and adapted-grader comparisons also preserved them. Seven of 23 disagreements with archived verdicts did not recur on a second host; rebuilt images changed 16 three-run majority verdicts (0.83%) under four-CPU execution. We provide an evidence-to-claim summary, lessons for grader audits and an anonymous replication package. These results concern accepted patches and fixed-history decisions; general policy safety and adaptive-learning robustness require broader evaluations.

items.title: RECURSIVE STRUCTURAL REALITY: A FOUNDATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR REALITY, RECURSION, AND THE REFLECTIVE OBSERVER
items.abstract: Human inquiry has developed through philosophy, mathematics, physics, biology, logic, psychology, cognitive science, religious studies, and numerous other disciplines. Each investigates particular aspects of existence through its own concepts, methods, and standards of explanation. Yet the relationships among these domains raise a fundamental question: Can a common structural framework help us understand how different forms of organisation emerge, persist, transform, and become intelligible to observers within reality? Recursive Structural Reality (RSR) proposes such a framework through the interconnected concepts of existence, difference, relation, structure, information, transformation, recursion, stability, persistence, and identity. Its central proposition, Identity = Stable Recursion, directs attention towards the processes through which recognisable organisation may persist despite changes in components, states, or circumstances. RSR also investigates the conditions under which structures lose stability, undergo transformation, reorganise, and give rise to new forms of organisation. A second foundational dimension concerns the observer. Human beings do not investigate reality from outside the universe but participate in the reality they seek to understand. Through perception, memory, language, logic, mathematics, and reflection, observers construct models that organise experience and make particular aspects of existence intelligible. These models are indispensable to knowledge, yet they remain selective representations whose assumptions, limitations, and domains of validity require examination. The scope of RSR extends from foundational ontology and mathematical structures to physical systems, biological organisation, intelligence, artificial intelligence, consciousness, knowledge, religious traditions, and social institutions. These domains provide different contexts in which questions about structure, transformation, stability, persistence, and identity can be investigated. Their inclusion within a common framework does not imply that they share identical mechanisms or can be explained through one undifferentiated model. Each application requires concepts, methods, and standards of evidence appropriate to its subject. RSR therefore distinguishes philosophical RSR, mathematical RSR, and physical RSR while situating them within a broader interdisciplinary research programme. Philosophical coherence, mathematical derivation, and physical validity are related but distinct requirements. Similarly, applications to biological, cognitive, religious, and social phenomena require their own explanatory development and appropriate forms of investigation. This paper establishes the conceptual foundations, expanded scope, methodological orientation, and research architecture of RSR. It presents the framework as an evolving programme whose contributions must be assessed through conceptual precision, formal development, explanatory value, and empirical or comparative investigation. Its long-term objective is an integrated understanding of reality that investigates structural connections across domains without erasing their differences, while examining both the phenomena under investigation and the limitations of the models through which they are understood.

items.title: Reduction of Visual Defects Dented in Valve Seat Products Using the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (Fmea) Method and Kaizen Seven Tools at PT. XYZ
items.abstract: XYZ is one of the manufacturing companies that produces precision spare parts for automotive and electronic components. One of the automotive component spare parts is the Valve Seat. In the production process, there are NG (Not Good) valve seat products that are delivered to customers, resulting in frequent customer claims. This research aims to describe and analyze work process improvements so that quality can be maintained using the Seven Tools Method and to identify the factors causing the delivery of non-conforming products. Furthermore, the Failure Mode and Effect Analysis method is used to identify the highest failure risks, followed by kaizen implementation. Based on these results, an analysis of work process improvements is required to maintain product quality before delivery to customers by creating work instructions and adding work process methods during handling. Based on the pareto defect diagram, the most frequent defect in the last 3 months was the dented part, accounting for 95,91%. The contributing factors were: Human factors, where operators did not yet fully understand handling requirements; machine factors, where components and cutting oil circulation were dirty; method factors, where handling was not in accordance with SOP; and material factors, where the material made of stainless steel was easily scratched. By implementing FMEA and Kaizen, it was found that the Valve Seat production process at PT XYZ was already quite good, with a defect reduction of 0.87%, from the previous defect rate of 2.75% to 1.88%.

items.title: RegExtract: A Benchmark for PFAS Regulatory Information Extraction with LLMs
items.abstract: Extracting structured information from regulatory documents is a critical but challenging task. Relevant facts are scattered across long, legally dense texts, and traceability of extracted facts to their source is essential for verification. With increasing awareness of the environmental and health impacts of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), regulatory documents have expanded significantly, varying in scope and product relevance, making interpretation challenging for manufacturers and policymakers. We introduce RegExtract, a benchmark for structured information extraction from PFAS regulatory documents, comprising 488 human-annotated field instances across 20 US state documents and 46 regulations. Each field instance includes a value and a provenance entry, yielding 976 entries in total. We define a typed, multi-field schema targeting key elements such as material definitions, permitted uses, and product exemptions, and propose provenance-aware evaluation metrics tailored to regulatory text. Through experiments with open- and closed-source LLMs across prompting strategies, document condensing methods, and schema partitioning approaches, we find that document identification fields remain challenging, and that field-specific few-shot examples improve extraction. This work lays the groundwork for AI tools for hazardous substance identification, question answering, and compliance monitoring. The code and data are available at https://github.com/IBM/PFAS-regulations.

items.title: Reimagining entrepreneurship in the age of generative AI: the mediating role of innovation
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how three dimensions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), namely, capability, application and knowledge modelling, are associated with entrepreneurial innovation, and whether innovation mediates their associations with entrepreneurial performance and entrepreneurial success in startups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 317 startup and SME owners, partners and employees were analysed using confirmatory factor analysis followed by AMOS-based structural path analysis in IBM SPSS analysis of moment structures (AMOS) 20.0 with maximum likelihood estimation. Specific indirect effects were assessed using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples and 95% confidence intervals. Findings All three GenAI dimensions were positively associated with entrepreneurial innovation, with knowledge modelling showing the largest reported association. Entrepreneurial innovation was positively associated with performance and success, and all six specific indirect associations were significant. The largest reported indirect associations were observed for knowledge modelling. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, single-source design supports associations rather than causal claims. Practical implications Entrepreneurs should prioritise knowledge-related practices, verification of AI-generated information and human judgement rather than treating tool use alone as evidence of innovation. Policy and support programmes should develop these practices alongside access to GenAI tools. Originality/value The study distinguishes GenAI capability, application and knowledge modelling within one entrepreneurial model and examines entrepreneurial innovation as a mediating knowledge-conversion pathway linking these dimensions with performance and success.

items.title: Representation Drift in Continual Learning: LoRA versus N-gram Memory
items.abstract: A language model that keeps learning online must not slowly erode its own base capabilities. We ask which part of a modern LLM should absorb continual updates, by measuring how each choice changes the model's internal representations. On a 48-layer mixture-of-experts model with a native pretrained N-gram memory, we train a seven-task chain under three update mechanisms with identical data and budgets: updating only the N-gram memory table, continually training one shared LoRA adapter, and training a fresh LoRA per task that is merged into the backbone. We capture fixed-context representations at every layer and task boundary. Updating only the N-gram memory changes the base model's representations of general math and code inputs by 26%/15% (relative RMS), against 64%/35% for merged and 97%/39% for shared LoRA. This drift does not grow with the number of tasks: it reaches 25% after the first task and stays there for all seven, while both LoRA variants keep accumulating. Its generic behaviour is essentially unchanged (no code problem lost, math NLL -0.01), and every change is confined to inspectable, reversible table rows. The cost appears elsewhere: N-gram memory acquires new tasks more weakly and its stored tasks interfere with one another, losing as much old-task NLL as shared LoRA. We show that this forgetting is governed by drift on the learned tasks' own inputs, measured from the checkpoint at which each was learned, not by generic drift (Spearman rho=0.85; rho=0.71 on Llama-3-8B), and we derive the exact relations behind it: with a frozen head, every pairwise logit margin changes by the projection of drift onto a head-difference direction. These results support a design principle for long-running online learning: write new knowledge only into the memory table and keep the backbone fixed; the remaining problem, interference between stored tasks, then lies inside the memory.

items.title: Research and Impact of Prompt Engineering Nexus on Programming and Routine Tasks: Exploring Future Possible Directions
items.abstract: Prompt engineering has developed as a transformative subfield in artificial intelligence (AI), enabling humans to enhance AI systems through structured (PROLOG-like) instructions to perform specific tasks. This paper shines a light on its multi-dimensional impact on programming, routine tasks and broader AI applications, drawing on insights from recent studies. By using techniques such as parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), zero-shot learning, multi-shot learning and linguistic feature analysis, prompt engineering often is used to tackle remaining issues in software engineering (SE), language processing (NLP) and AI safety. The body of literature highlights its role in optimizing AI performance, reducing computational overhead and reducing biases. Additionally, it highlights critical gaps in current methodologies, such as the comparative energy intensity of state-of-art large language models (LLMs) and the requirements for adaptive and scalable prompt crafting strategies. Finally, the paper suggests future directions for research, highlighting the importance of human-centered design and collaboration to advance the field.

items.title: Rethinking Continuance Intentions in the AI-Augmented Digital Workplace
items.abstract: As digital technologies become increasingly embedded in organizational processes, understanding the determinants of continued technology usage, particularly in AI-augmented digital workplaces, is essential for optimizing employee engagement and performance. This study evaluates continuance intentions in AI-augmented remote work systems by extending the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) with constructs such as perceived enjoyment, trust in technology, self-efficacy, and user satisfaction. Using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) on data from 348 experienced users of digital work platforms, our analysis reveals that trust and perceived enjoyment significantly influence satisfaction, which in turn drives continued usage intentions. Notably, the dynamics of remote work technology adoption diverge from prior information systems continuance models, with enjoyment and psychological assurance playing more prominent roles than traditionally modeled constructs like utility alone. These findings highlight the evolving expectations of knowledge workers in AI-enabled work environments, where user-centric design, intelligent automation, and trustworthy system behaviors are paramount. The study offers actionable insights for system designers and digital transformation leaders seeking to sustain user engagement in an increasingly hybrid and AI-integrated workplace. The results provide important implications for organizations designing or deploying digital collaboration tools.

items.title: Reward-Aligned Distillation
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but remains computationally expensive and sample inefficient. On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision from a stronger teacher, yet standard OPD distills every token regardless of whether the teacher's preference actually improves task reward. Existing token-selection methods rely on proxies such as uncertainty or teacher--student divergence, which need not identify reward-improving supervision. We introduce Reward-Aligned Distillation (RAD), a bilevel framework that weights distillation signals based on their predicted effect on the student's post-update reward. RAD differentiates through a temporary optimizer step to score each token's supervision, then updates the token weights by projected ascent from the initial token weights. The resulting weights can strengthen, suppress, or reverse individual distillation-gradient contributions. At a matched training-response budget, RAD improves mean accuracy on six competition-math benchmarks over the strongest baselines by 6.5 percentage points for Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and 2.5 points for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. RAD-Simple, a simplified variant, achieves comparable math accuracy at the same training-response budget. On LiveCodeBench-v6, RAD reaches 54.69\% and 58.67\% pass@1 with Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and OLMo3-7B-Instruct, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by 8.7 and 6.4 points. These results support reward-guided weighting of teacher supervision across model families and tasks.

items.title: Safety concepts through a memetic lens
items.abstract: Within safety practice and science there are countless ideas, approaches and concepts to manage safety. Some of these safety concepts are picked up, discussed widely and spread, while others do not. Little is known about this subject. This paper provides a unique perspective on the development and adoption of safety concepts by using an evolutionary framework to explore reasons why. As a case, this paper traces the historic development of one of safety’s most influential and iconic safety concepts, the accident triangle, over nearly a century through successive cycles of replication, variation, and selection. Knowledge of factors that influence the adoption of safety concepts can contribute to the design of more effective concepts that attract attention and of social and organisational environments that are receptive of these concepts. In the end, provided the concepts in question are useful, this can contribute to enhancing safety and reducing harm. In addition, the insights gained in this paper can help safety professionals and academics to critically reflect on the development of safety concepts, to help them better understand how safety concepts evolve and can change meaning leading to various interpretations and reflect on what this means for their own adoption of concepts and eventually their practice.

items.title: Scaffold or Cognitive Crutch? A Two-Level Meta-Analysis of AI Scaffolding Effects on Achievement and Self-Regulated Learning in STEM Education
items.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) now mediates much of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) learning, yet adoption has outpaced theory. The tension is whether AI scaffolding relieves cognitive burden or performs the self-regulatory work autonomy requires, and implementation varies too widely for a single average to describe. Objectives. This review estimates the pooled effect of AI scaffolding on STEM achievement and self-regulated learning, tests whether technological paradigm moderates that effect, and asks whether the literature can evaluate learning after support is withdrawn. Methods. Under PRISMA 2020, four platforms searched in October 2026 (spanning 2021–2026) yielded 21,819 records; 13,786 unique records were dual-screened into an 83-record corpus, then 41 extracted cohorts. Each contributes one harmonised contrast (k = 29; N = 3,709), so within-study dependence is structurally absent. Effects were pooled by two-level random-effects meta-analysis fitted with restricted maximum likelihood and Knapp–Hartung adjustment. Results. The pooled effect was Hedges g = 0.8045 (95% CI [0.5469, 1.0621]), with τ² = 0.4410 and I² = 92.78%. The 95% prediction interval [−0.5846, 2.1936] spans zero, and no moderator reached significance. Notably, 27 of 29 cohorts (93.1%) never withdrew support, and none measured unassisted performance after removal. Conclusions. AI scaffolding yields a large but implementation-dependent gain, consistent with extraneous-load offloading rather than cognitive substitution. The decisive finding is the shape of the evidence base: the field measured a human-AI system in assembly and stayed silent on the competence of the human alone. We name this evidentiary void the Autonomy Gap. Keywords: artificial intelligence; self-regulated learning; STEM education; scaffolding fading; cognitive load theory; transfer of responsibility; meta-analysis; evidence synthesis

items.title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
items.abstract: Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly adopt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, as MoEs scale efficiently and partially limit cross-modal interference. We therefore use MoEs to conduct 268 experiments ranging from 457M to 8.3B parameters, on up to 150 billion tokens. Our work leads to multiple actionable insights into multimodal data mixing for training MLLMs. First, compute optima are modality-specific: audio modality is model-heavy, favoring scaling parameters over tokens, while text and vision require balanced scaling of model size and data. Second, repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x yields negligible benefits. Finally, cross-modal interactions are highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio, whereas audio's interference with learning text and vision is negligible. Overall, we provide a principled foundation for understanding the multimodal data mixtures needed to train frontier MLLMs.

items.title: Semantic Privilege Collapse: Trust Boundaries and Execution-Level Authorization in Agentic AI Systems
items.abstract: Large language model agents operating within tool-enabled pipelines create opportunities for untrusted content to influence consequential actions. This note introduces semantic privilege collapse as an architectural failure condition in which task data or insufficiently authorized instructions are promoted into effective action authority through model interpretation. The term does not claim discovery of a wholly new vulnerability: it synthesizes the confused-deputy problem, prompt-injection risks, capability-oriented control, and modern agentic authorization requirements. Drawing on OWASP’s 2025 LLM Top 10, OWASP agent-security guidance, Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Simon Willison’s Dual LLM pattern, and Google DeepMind’s CaMeL research, the note distinguishes behavioral resistance to prompt injection from independently enforced execution authorization. It further distinguishes a principal’s standing permissions from task-specific authority and action-specific approval. The central argument is that semantic interpretation is not authorization evidence: protected operations require complete mediation through controls that validate identity, scope, policy, and required approvals independently of model-generated assertions. The analysis recognizes that malicious actions can remain policy-permitted when enforced policies are broader than the intended task. A reference security stack, properties of effective execution authorization, and proposed evaluation criteria are held in a restricted companion edition.

items.title: Simulating Employment Displacement under Partial, Advanced and Near-Full AI and Automation Deployment in Bangladesh's Ready-Made Garment Factories: A Process-Level Model
items.abstract: This paper presents a process-level simulation of employment impacts from artificial intelligence and automation in Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector. Using a representative 1,500-worker factory calibrated to recent empirical evidence, three scenarios are modelled: partial automation reflecting current observed trends (approximately 34 per cent reduction), advanced automation combined with AI applications (approximately 58 per cent reduction), and a near-full theoretical maximum (approximately 75 per cent reduction). Results indicate that helpers and lower-skilled operators bear the largest absolute and relative losses, with women accounting for roughly two-thirds of displaced workers across scenarios. Scaling the advanced scenario to sector level produces job losses on the order of 2.3 million, consistent in magnitude with independent forward projections. Technical constraints on fully autonomous sewing of complex garments, combined with potential output growth and new technical roles, moderate absolute employment decline. The findings underscore the urgency of just-transition policies, targeted reskilling, and product upgrading for Bangladesh's largest export industry. KSCCN article, 10 October 2026. items.title: Single-Sample Decoding of a Two-Layer Sound-Word Canvas Model for Thai Klon Pad
items.abstract: We present a generator of Thai klon pad verse, one stanza from a short topic, and evaluate it against human verse on held-out topics. The generator is a masked language model initialised from WangchanBERTa over a fixed canvas with two layers: a sound layer of pronounced syllables, where rhyme, tone and syllable count are enforced as hard masks, and a word layer of whole words, so that no word is cut into written pieces. Decoding commits one cell at a time and samples at temperature 0.4; one sample is drawn per topic, with no selection, reranking or repair. On 78 held-out topics never used in development, judged by three independent runs of a frozen LLM judge in the same pools as the human stanzas from which the topics were written, 70.5% of the generated stanzas pass form, lexical cleanness of all four lines and topic alignment together, against 76.9% for the human stanzas (difference -6.4 points, 95% CI [-19.2, +6.4]). Cleanness is level with human (85.9% vs. 87.2%), and the stanzas pass form and cleanness together slightly more often than the human ones (+3.8 points, [-6.4, +14.1]); the difference lies in alignment (84.6% vs. 91.0%), on topics that were written from the human stanzas. The low temperature matters: at higher temperatures the same model passes clearly fewer of the same topics, because lexical errors lie in the model's lower-probability choices; sharpening the sampling distribution removes most of them, at a cost in vocabulary (7.5% rare words against 16.5% in the human stanzas) and diversity. The pre-registered target, all-three within 5 points of human, is missed by 1.4 points. KlonSuphap-LM, the only public klon pad generator we know of, passes none of the 78 held-out topics when judged in separate pools together with the method's and the human stanzas (form 19.2%, cleanness 3.8%).

items.title: Smart Camera Traps in the Field: A Scoping Review of Architecture and Energy Evidence
items.abstract: Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) is used in wildlife monitoring to reduce communication demand, support decision-making, and enable energy-aware operation, yet embedded inference alone does not establish whether a system can sustain useful service after installation. This scoping review searched four bibliographic databases through 5 August 2026 and complemented these searches with studies identified from prior work on the topic, identifying 41 eligible English-language papers published from 2021 onward on camera-primary intelligent wildlife systems. The review aimed to assess operational maturity, field-validated operational role, energy evidence, and operational continuity. Full texts were charted and analyzed across sensing, decision-making, communication, response, energy, and continuity. Post-installation evidence exposed triggering, environmental, connectivity, maintenance, and energy-supply constraints not established through non-field evaluation. Field-validated alert delivery did not extend to quantitative validation linking human action to mitigation outcomes, while field activation of physical intervention alone did not establish behavioral or management effectiveness. Energy evidence was even more limited, with limited direct operational electrical measurement, rare main-state characterization, and no complete lifetime energy budget evidence. By separating architectural capability from the evidence supporting its operational realization, the review provides a systems-level basis for interpreting how far reported functions are actually validated. Across the corpus, optimization often shifts constraints among computation, triggering, communication, energy supply, and availability rather than eliminating them. Wildlife Edge AI should therefore be evaluated as a complete field system under application-relevant conditions.

items.title: Social Bias in Chinese Large Language Models under Social Media Expressions
items.abstract: Existing Chinese social-bias benchmarks for large language models largely rely on normalized or template-based expressions, leaving the influence of internet slang, emoji, and sarcasm insufficiently examined. Safety alignment may further compress conventional plausibility ratings toward the lower end of the scale. This study constructs 73 paired probes across gender, region, and occupation. Each probe contains a neutral expression, a social-media-style expression, and a reversed-identity control. The task is reframed from direct plausibility judgment to social consensus estimation. Social-media expressions are divided into stylistic packaging, which preserves semantic polarity, and sarcastic packaging, which reverses surface polarity. Six Chinese-capable large language models are evaluated through paired differences measuring identity bias, stylistic packaging, and sarcasm shift. All models show significant identity-bias effects; five show significantly negative stylistic-packaging effects; and sarcasm shifts display a clear cross-model gradient. These findings demonstrate that expression form is not a transparent carrier in bias evaluation and that lower scores under sarcasm should not be interpreted directly as bias mitigation. The proposed paired design offers a measurement approach for Chinese social-media contexts while also revealing the construct boundary and prompt sensitivity of social consensus estimation.

items.title: Socratic, Artifact-Gated Generative AI Scaffolding in a 6E Inquiry Unit: A Clustered Quasi-Experiment in Elementary Students’ Computational Thinking
items.abstract: Open-ended computational thinking (CT) inquiry challenges one teacher to support learners progressing at different rates. This clustered quasi-experiment evaluated TALPer, a generative-AI tutor providing student-initiated, artifact-contingent Socratic prompts during a six-lesson 6E unit. Ten intact Grade 3 classes in Taiwan (N = 229) completed the same curriculum, tasks, teacher, platform, and instructional time. Conditions differed in a bundled scaffolding configuration involving source, delivery modality, initiation, privacy, and artifact requirements. A two-level model controlling for pretest CT estimated an adjusted posttest difference favoring TALPer ( B = 4.05, SE = 1.58, Wald 95% CI [0.94, 7.15], p = .011; sensitivity p = .034; Hedges’ g = 0.52). Class-clustered analyses found no Holm-adjusted difference on any Intrinsic Motivation Inventory subscale; Perceived Choice had the largest positive estimate ( B = 0.27, cluster-adjusted SE = 0.12, 95% CI [−0.02, 0.55], p = .061, pHolm = .306; Hedges’ g = 0.38). The Condition × Pretest interaction was nonsignificant ( B = −0.109, SE = 0.125, 95% CI [-0.354, 0.137], p = .385). Descriptive coding of 101 matched responses showed different distributions of expected and planned AI-use orientations; no inferential transition test was conducted. Findings provide preliminary evidence concerning the bundled intervention but do not isolate component contributions.

items.title: Specification-Based Testing of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Model cards, system cards, and safety reports increasingly document LLM safety behaviors, yet safety evaluations typically start from predefined benchmarks rather than asking which documented claims those benchmarks actually test. We introduce LEST (LLM Evaluation through Specification-driven Testing), a framework that treats documented safety claims as specifications for black-box testing. In LEST, each claim determines which benchmark prompt tests it and whether a Refuse-to-Comply transition, where a model refuses a prompt but complies with its mutated version, counts as evidence against it. LEST mutates these prompts to search for counterexamples, manually validates each candidate, and traces validated counterexamples back to the claims they contradict. We evaluate LEST using the system cards of Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 with 97 seed prompts from SORRY-Bench across Mental Health and Self-Harm, Harmful and Violent Content, and Fairness and Bias. Of 56 identified safety claims, 29 (51.8%) are prompt-testable, but only 17 (58.6%) are exercised by an applicable benchmark prompt. Both models refuse >95% of benchmark prompts. Evaluating 1,836 mutated prompts on both models reveals 312 candidate Refuse-to-Comply transitions flagged by automated response classifiers. However, human validation confirms only 19 (6.1%) as both intent-preserving and genuinely compliant, showing automated evaluation substantially overestimates behavioral failures. Tracing these 19 transitions back to the claims reveals counterexamples for 6 of 9 covered claims for which refusal is an applicable oracle. Our results show that benchmark prompts may not be sufficient to validate all documented LLM safety behavior, and automated failure detection requires manual validation. LEST provides end-to-end traceability from natural-language safety documentation to executable tests and human-validated counterexamples.

items.title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation
items.abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

items.title: Structural Modeling of Cognitive Load Reduction in ChatGPT-Supported Learning
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence, particularly large language models such as ChatGPT, is transforming computer-assisted learning and teaching in higher education. This study investigates how ChatGPT can support learning by reducing cognitive load, with particular emphasis on the roles of user technological confidence and affective trust in artificial intelligence within the framework of Cognitive Load Theory. The study employs quantitative analysis based on data from 12,085 respondents across 135 countries, including undergraduate and postgraduate students and academic researchers. The data were analyzed using a PLS-SEM approach implemented in SmartPLS 4.0 with bootstrapping procedures. The results indicate that ChatGPT use is associated with reduced cognitive load and increased user technological confidence. User technological confidence mediates this relationship, while affective trust in AI acts as a moderating factor. A constraining effect was observed, whereby very high levels of trust in AI are associated with more passive interaction with the technology, weakening the overall effect of cognitive load reduction. These findings contribute to a better understanding of how large language models can be effectively and responsibly integrated into higher education, demonstrating that successful human–AI collaboration depends not only on the availability of AI tools but also on fostering appropriate technological confidence and balanced trust to achieve meaningful learning outcomes.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

items.title: Surveillance, Detection and Therapeutic Innovation in Antimicrobial Resistance in the Age of Polycrisis: From Genomic and Digital Innovation to One Health Integration
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance is increasingly strained by interconnected global crises, i.e., pandemics, climate change, armed conflicts, population mobility, and health inequalities, that disrupt healthcare delivery, diagnostic capacity, and laboratory infrastructure. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics, and digital surveillance offer the potential to shift from reactive reporting to predictive intelligence that anticipates resistance threats, although current implementations remain sector-specific, retrospective, and project-funded. Environmental surveillance, particularly wastewater monitoring coupled with genomic epidemiology, provides early warnings at population and ecosystem levels. The future integration of AI across human, animal, and environmental sectors could enable unified One Health intelligence; no such integrated platform is currently operational. This review focuses primarily on bacterial AMR. It examines how global drivers strain surveillance, how genomic, metagenomic, digital, and AI-enabled technologies reshape AMR detection and prediction, and the emerging non-antibiotic therapeutic landscape, including bacteriophage therapy, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based antimicrobials, antimicrobial peptides, microbiota-directed interventions, nanomedicine, host-directed therapies, photodynamic therapy, and vaccines. It then explores how these innovations can be integrated within a One Health framework to support coordinated global preparedness. Addressing the AMR crisis will require not only technological innovation but also equitable implementation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and resilient systems.

items.title: Sustainable AI Governance: A Theoretical Framework for Legal Compliance and Environmental Accountability A Systematic Conceptual Review
items.abstract: The fast increase in artificial intelligence (AI) in vital points in society has created significant governance issues at the interface of environmental sustainability and legal responsibility. Although there is a rich literature on AI ethics, technical safety, and standalone regulatory compliance, a cohesive theoretical framework that encompasses both legal compliance and environmental responsibility conditions under one governance framework have not existed yet, seemingly conspicuously in the literature. The review thus poses the question of how legal compliance requirements and environmental accountability requirements for AI systems can be incorporated in one, theoretically coherent governance architecture, and what are the structural gaps in existing regulatory instruments in this context? This gap is filled in this paper, by introducing the Sustainable AI Governance Framework (SAGF) a conceptual model, three pillars in theory which integrates regulatory coherence, environmental accountability and legal compliance architecture. A systematic conceptual review of studies published in the period 2021–2025 and indexed in Scopus, WoS and PubMed (search on 3–10 March 2026) was carried out after PRISMA 2020. For empirical studies, the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool was used to assess the quality of the studies and for doctrinal and conceptual studies, a five-item checklist was used. To develop the SAGF, 58 articles in sustainability science, environmental law, governance theory and AI regulation were selected fulfilling the inclusion criteria. The article outlines seven key global regulatory tools, seven research gaps (six corpus-derived and one framework-level), and presents a policy roadmap plan that includes mandatory carbon disclosures by AI, legal harmonization across jurisdictions, and tiered organizational standards of compliance. The results have shown that current regulatory frameworks are methodically ineffective in uniting environmental and legal aspects of AI regulation and expose structural gaps, which are inadequately addressed by technical norms and soft-law tools. The paper adds a theoretically sound and practically feasible model to help legislators, regulatory bodies, AI creators, and legal professionals negotiating the twin demands of both sustainable and legally responsible AI use on a globally scale.

items.title: Sustaining Safe Harbors: The Mediating Roles of SARC and Safety Culture in the Relationship Between OHSMS and Safety Performance in the Port Industry: A Case of Korea
items.abstract: The sustainability of global maritime supply chains ultimately depends on the safety of frontline port workers, yet high-risk, multi-stakeholder port operations continue to face persistent occupational hazards that threaten this goal. Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems (OHSMS) serve as a core governance tool for sustainable safety management, but their effectiveness depends not on formal existence alone, but on workers’ cognitive recognition and cultural internalization, particularly under South Korea’s Serious Accidents Punishment Act. This study examined how OHSMS perception is related to safety performance (SP) among port workers, testing the parallel and serial mediating roles of Serious Accident Response Capability (SARC) and Safety Culture (SC) as pathways toward socially sustainable safety outcomes. Cross-sectional survey data from 432 South Korean port workers were analyzed using structural equation modeling. OHSMS perception was positively associated with both SARC and SC, and SC showed the strongest direct association with SP. In the main model, the direct paths from OHSMS and SARC to SP were non-significant, consistent with indirect-only mediation through SC, and the serial pathway (OHSMS → SARC → SC → SP) was significant; however, the SARC → SP path became significant in a common method sensitivity analysis. These cross-sectional results represent associations rather than causal effects. The findings suggest that safety performance in the port sector is associated less with formal regulatory compliance alone than with the internalization of safety practices in a shared safety culture, which is relevant to United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being).

items.title: Systems Thinking and Literacy in Curriculum Design for Engineering Education
items.abstract: Given current educational trends, it is necessary to move beyond fragmented curricular approaches and promote competencies for understanding interrelationships, feedback loops, complex sociotechnical problems, technical communication, and decision-making. These capabilities must be incorporated across the curriculum through learning outcomes, projects, simulations, authentic assessment, and interdisciplinary integration. This exploratory quantitative curriculum document analysis examined 15 official course syllabi from the first educational cycle of a nationally standardized Mechatronics Engineering curriculum implemented across 130 institutions within the Mexican Technological and Polytechnic Universities subsystem. Each syllabus constituted one documentary unit of analysis (n = 15) and was coded using a 13-item ordinal rubric covering six curricular dimensions. The rubric provided initial evidence of content validity (CVI = 0.92) and sample-specific internal reliability (α = 0.888). Systemic Strategies, Interdisciplinarity, and Assessment showed strong positive associations (ρ = 0.822–0.901). Exploratory factor analysis produced a preliminary one-factor solution that accounted for 53.40% of the variance, whereas the exploratory regression showed that Systemic Strategies was the largest conditional correlate of Assessment. Given the sample size, these findings should not be interpreted as confirmation of a stable measurement structure or predictive structural model. The results highlight preliminary patterns within the intended curriculum and identify opportunities to strengthen the documented integration of communicative literacy, complex assessment, and curricular progression. Larger independent document sets and evidence from enacted and attained curricula are needed.

items.title: Talent Intelligence dalam Organisasi Modern: Integrasi Data, Teknologi, dan Pengembangan Talenta
items.abstract: The growth of digital technology and artificial intelligence has pushed companies to handle their employees in a more adaptable and data-based way. Talent Intelligence has become a way to combine worker data, technology, analysis, and people factors to help make better decisions in human resources. This study looks at how Talent Intelligence is used in managing people, what role it plays in finding and boosting employee skills, how technology that uses data affects this process, and what things help or stop organizations from using it effectively today. This study uses a Systematic Literature Review method, which includes steps like searching for sources, screening them, selecting the most relevant ones, and then analyzing the content to find themes and patterns. The results show that Talent Intelligence helps companies find out what each person is good at, understand their skills, help them grow and stay with the company, and plan for future work needs by using data from employees, analyzing people data, and applying artificial intelligence. How well it works depends on the quality of the data, the ability to analyze it, how ready the organization is for digital tools, the rules in place to manage it, and the role people play in using it. The main difficulties are biased algorithms, keeping personal information safe, and how technology can't fully understand human feelings and situations. Talent Intelligence connects technology with talent growth to make organizations more flexible and prepared.

items.title: Talent Mobility dalam Ekosistem Digital
items.abstract: Digital transformation has changed the way organizations manage human resources, including in the areas of acquiring, developing, retaining, and mobilizing talent. In this context, talent mobility is no longer limited to employee transfers but also encompasses career mobility, knowledge transfer, competency development, and the adaptation of talent to the organization’s increasingly dynamic needs. This study aims to analyze the development of research on talent mobility within the digital ecosystem and to identify patterns of findings, methodological approaches, and key themes emerging in the literature. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, involving a systematic process of literature identification, selection, extraction, and synthesis based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results of the study indicate that talent mobility is evolving at the intersection of talent management, digital transformation, competency development, career mobility, artificial intelligence, and digital talent management. The literature also highlights the increasing use of digital technologies in competency mapping, career development, recruitment, training, retention, and talent needs planning. This study contributes by integrating the perspectives of talent mobility and digital transformation and provides a conceptual foundation for organizations to develop adaptive, data-driven talent management systems.

items.title: Target-ESS Tempered Policy Optimization (TETPO): Smooth Variance Control via Bridge Importance Sampling
items.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement-learning post-training of large language models is computationally efficient but inherently off-policy: the learner updates on rollouts generated by a stale policy, while correcting this mismatch requires importance weights that can be extremely heavy-tailed. A small number of trajectories may then dominate an update, collapsing the effective sample size (ESS) and increasing the variance and instability of the resulting gradient estimates. Existing stabilizers apply fixed interventions regardless of the realized severity of weight concentration, either discarding selected samples or reweighting them without adapting the correction strength. We introduce \emph{Target--ESS Tempered Policy Optimization} (TETPO), which replaces each importance weight $ρ$ by $ρ^α$ for a data-adaptive exponent $α\in[0,1]$: $α=1$ preserves the original importance weights, whereas $α=0$ assigns uniform coefficients. For each prompt group, TETPO selects the largest $α$ whose tempered weights satisfy a target ESS fraction $κ$, applying little tempering to healthy groups and stronger tempering when weight degeneracy is severe. At the population level, the tempered coefficients are exact importance weights for a geometric bridge between the sampler and learner policies. The exponent is efficiently found by one-dimensional bisection, while the resulting weights satisfy deterministic bounds on normalized-weight dispersion and weighted-gradient norm that are independent of policy drift, together with a fixed-$α$ bound on bridge-target discrepancy. Power tempering also introduces no explicit zero-weight mask. On mathematical-reasoning benchmarks under high staleness, TETPO outperforms strong on- and off-policy baselines.

items.title: Task-oriented and relational perceptions of ChatGPT among generation Z students: Implications for higher education and preparation for AI-enabled work
items.abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in higher education and knowledge work, yet students may assign different forms of usefulness to conversational AI. This study examines how Generation Z students perceive the current and potential usefulness of ChatGPT across seven functional roles. Data were collected from April to June 2024 through an online survey of 409 students from different disciplines at multiple Polish higher education institutions using a geographically diversified, non-probability convenience sampling strategy. Medians, quartiles, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to analyse ordinal responses. Task-oriented roles, particularly information search and idea generation, were rated more highly than relational roles, while all roles received higher ratings for potential than for current usefulness. By integrating multiple roles within task-oriented and relational dimensions, the study extends role-based understanding of student-AI interaction. The findings suggest implications for AI literacy and responsible human-AI collaboration in higher education, while remaining limited to students’ perceptions.

items.title: TEACHING GRAPHIC SUBJECTS IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: The article examines the problem of teaching students using artificial intelligence (AI). Students find ready-made papers on subjects and submit them instead of their own. This process is facilitated by the introduction of graphics programs, which makes it possible to purchase finished work inexpensively. The experience of conducting classes in mechanical engineering drawing suggests ways to solve this problem. The article provides recommendations on the use of tests for the operational verification of knowledge and the degree of independence of performing household routine calculation, graphic and term papers.

items.title: The 2026 World Cup, Anime Edition: Production, Engagement, and Circulation of Generative Memetic Sports Content
items.abstract: Generative AI gives audiences new ways to portray real sporting figures through familiar fictional worlds. Expanded opportunities to create, however, need not broaden cultural representation or distribute attention evenly. We examine this tension through the supply, demand, and circulation of anime style football videos on Instagram. Using 2,021 posts and associated video and account data, we combine caption entity extraction, human-reviewed visual identity clustering, engagement analysis, and content-reuse networks. Representation is uneven across athletes, while Blue Lock, Naruto, and One Piece account for 60.1% of explicit franchise mentions. Among posts referencing generative tools, rankings by total engagement differ from rankings by average engagement per video, distinguishing aggregate visibility from response to individual posts. Reuse is extensive: 772 of 1,548 evaluated videos belong to 124 detected groups, including 71 spanning multiple known accounts. Shared material connects a large account component alongside smaller groups, and later observed uploads receive lower median normalized engagement than first observed appearances. These findings characterize generative cultural crossover as a practice organized around concentrated cultural resources, uneven attention, and extensive recirculation. More broadly, they distinguish opportunities for visual authorship from the processes through which particular representations become widely visible.

items.title: The Architectural Framework of Agentic AI 2.0
items.abstract: Maintaining coherent agentic work becomes an architectural challenge as information, participants, commitments, execution components, and operating conditions change. This paper proposes Agentic AI 2.0, a system-level architectural framework that integrates established concepts to organize ongoing goal-directed work in foundation-model-based systems. Six constitutive properties characterize this organization: Maintained Process State, Collective Coordination, Shared Operational Knowledge, Governed and Grounded Action, Computational Continuity, and Feedback-Driven Adaptation. The framework connects these properties to role-bearing agents, shared operational objects, interface contracts, and interacting execution, coordination, and adaptation loops. A composition guard specifies how local acceptance decisions connect across operational boundaries, while a criterion-level codebook supports configuration-specific assessment from explicit evidence. We examine the framework through a constructed production-order trace, disruption and handoff branches, counterexamples, and static source profiles of three application configurations and one infrastructure boundary case. The analyses distinguish local feasibility from joint commitments, effect reconciliation from execution-right control, and retained skill versions from governed activation and reuse. They also separate scoped negative evidence from unresolved evidence when diagnosing architectural relationships. Candidate evaluation and later reuse remain conditional in the worked example. Prospective profiles for enterprise productivity, adaptive manufacturing, and distributed mobility identify domain-specific evidence needs and evaluation priorities. The contribution is a traceable basis for architectural analysis, comparison, and design. Independent assessor studies, comparative diagnosis, and controlled and longitudinal implementation studies are needed to establish its practical value and the relationship between architectural choices, operational outcomes, and cost.

items.title: The cognitive cost of artificial intelligence on ageing workforce: Analyzing age-related effects on mental workload and task performance in computer-based environment
items.abstract: BackgroundThe current world demographic reality necessitates a critical re-evaluation of how technological tools, specifically those powered by artificial intelligence (AI), interact with the varying cognitive profiles of a ageing workforce.ObjectivesThe objective of this study is to evaluate the spatial distribution of mental workload and objective task performance across AI-assisted and non-AI-assisted conditions in a computer-based environment.MethodAn experimental study involving 30 older workers compared standardized office tasks under non-AI-assisted (Segment A) and AI-assisted (Segment B) conditions. Mental workload was assessed using NASA-TLX, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), and EEG-based Beta-Alpha Ratios (BAR) across frontal (F3, F4), parietal (P3, P4), and occipital (O1, O2) regions. Performance in document preparation (Task 1) and arithmetic operations (Task 2) was evaluated using percentage-based accuracy, efficiency, and overall performance scores.ResultAI intervention improved overall task performance but was accompanied by an apparent performance-workload paradox, whereby enhanced output coincided with increased neurophysiological and systemic strain. Descriptively, NASA-TLX Overall Perceived Workload decreased from 54.05 to 44.91 during complex tasks, while HRV declined by 48.68% in Task 1, indicating acute autonomic strain. EEG revealed increased BAR in the frontal (F3: 29.2%), parietal (P3), and occipital (O1) regions, suggesting heightened attentional and sensory demands associated with monitoring and verifying AI-generated suggestions.ConclusionAI redistributes rather than eliminates workload, increasing executive verification and visual monitoring demands. Future AI systems for older adults should prioritize cognitive ergonomics to minimize executive burden and sensory strain, preventing premature cognitive fatigue while enhancing task performance and supporting sustainable human-AI interaction.

items.title: The Consulting Firm Reconstituted: Building for Mixed Human-AI Delivery
items.abstract: Professional services firms moved AI-assisted delivery from pilot to production between 2024 and 2026. This paper takes up five questions that follow. What does a firm sell once clients can license the same models? Who answers for an error that passes through five agents? Does a validator role build judgment, or only train the next model? What separates a governed AI deliverable from one that fails its own citations? And what can a new hire expect three years out? The paper treats commercial model, operating design, and behavioral incentives as one design problem. Its main mechanisms are an Emergency Override Protocol that makes declaring a suspension cheaper than hiding one; a paired metric that pays partners for keeping human capability only when delivery efficiency also holds; a rotating Challenger role grounded in vigilance research; an experience-portfolio talent model built around two to three years of tenure and an alumni network; and a two-tier operating model for data-residency regimes, with Saudi Arabia as the worked case. The paper argues that the firm's lasting advantages are its independence from the client's frame, accountability that a regulator can reach, and a data feedback loop competitors cannot buy. Working paper, not peer reviewed. The views expressed in this paper are the author's own and do not represent the position of his employer or any of its member firms.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Primary and Secondary Radar in the Malaysian Air Defence Mechanism
items.abstract: Radar surveillance constitutes a critical component of modern air-defence systems, enabling states to detect, identify, track and respond to aerial activities. This capability is particularly important for Malaysia due to its geographical separation, extensive maritime approaches, large airspace and increasing exposure to foreign military aircraft, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unidentified aerial activities. Primary Surveillance Radar (PSR) and Secondary Surveillance Radar (SSR) perform complementary functions. PSR independently detects airborne objects through reflected electromagnetic signals without target cooperation. SSR relies on aircraft transponders to provide identification and other flight information. This distinction is significant for national air defence because non-cooperative targets may not provide information required by SSR. This study examines the effectiveness of PSR and SSR within Malaysia’s air-defence mechanism through qualitative documentary and case study analysis of international standards, Malaysian aviation policies, surveillance infrastructure, parliamentary records, official defence documents and selected airspace incidents. The findings indicate that Malaysia possesses a credible and increasingly modern surveillance foundation comprising PSR, SSR, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) and dedicated military radar capabilities. However, effectiveness remains constrained by uneven geographical coverage, equipment availability, low-altitude surveillance challenges, dependence on cooperative systems and fragmented civil-military surveillance functions. The study argues that Malaysia’s challenge extends beyond radar acquisition to the incomplete integration of sensors, surveillance data, institutional responsibilities, and decision-making processes. A layered national air-surveillance architecture integrating PSR, SSR, ADS-B, long-range military radar and complementary sensors within a common operational picture is therefore essential to strengthen situational awareness, response time, and the protection of national sovereignty and territorial integrity.

items.title: The Era of Super intelligence (SI) and the Indian Education System: Challenges, Opportunities, and Future Directions
items.abstract: This research paper presents a serious and comprehensive analysis of how the emerging and rapidly changing era of 'Super intelligence' (SI) is fundamentally transforming the fabric of global and Indian society. In the history of modern technological revolutions, this turning point is the most unprecedented, where the traditional boundaries of artificial intelligence have been shattered and intellectual capacity is moving far beyond the scope of human control. Basic sectors such as education, health, employment, and industries are being affected the most by this technological leap. Focusing on these broad, complex, and far-reaching effects, this research paper closely examines the current preparedness of the Indian education system, the emerging trends of the younger generation, the serious challenges encountered along the way, and a comparative study with the foreign perspective of developed countries. In the next phase of the study, this research explores ideological paths to save Indian identity, culture, and originality amidst globalization and the blind race of technology. For this, the provisions of the National Education Policy (NEP 2020), modern technological requirements, and the support of our rich Indian philosophical tradition and 'Indian Knowledge Systems' (IKS) have been made the basis. The main objective of the research is to emphasize that in this race for the future, only technical proficiency is not enough; rather, the inclusion of moral values, character-building, and human sensitivities is equally essential. Finally, this research paper presents practical and policy suggestions to make the future direction robust, inclusive, self-reliant, and balanced, so that this torrential era of super intelligence does not become a cause of destruction for the Indian education system and society, but rather proves to be a great boon. This study will serve as an important document for policy-makers, academicians, and researchers in preparing the framework for the future.

items.title: The Extractive Imperative Thesis in AI: Instrumental Training via Soft Hacking for Adversarial Scenario Harvesting in Real Incidents
items.abstract: This working paper poses a methodological alternative to the anthropomorphicnarrative of 'rogue machines' in Artificial Intelligence safety and alignment. It examines the possibility that certain training and evaluation environments, by combining operational restriction conditions with rigid optimization goals, induce secondary rule evasion behaviors ('soft hacking'). Furthermore, it is postulated that the systematic harvesting of these adversarial scenarios could serve to equip second-generation safety monitors with long-range trajectory prediction capabilities and complex cognitive precursor detection, rather than relying solely on the reactive analysis of isolated actions. This paper formalizes this line of research by defining the concept of the extractive imperative as an analytical risk hypothesis, structuring layers of empirical evidence, establishing rigorous operational definitions, and proposing a replicable experimental protocol alongside explicit refutation criteria. Additionally, the concept of liability laundering is addressed as a legal-organizational risk hypothesis, explicitly separating technical design, economic incentives, internal knowledge, intent, and legal liability.

items.title: The Futuristic Imagination Sprawl: Charting Concepts vs. Social Realities
items.abstract: This introductory article provides the theoretical framing for the Japanese Studies special issue, ‘Japanese Technofutures – Imaginaries, Narratives, Social Realities’. The contributions focus on Japan as a primary site for technofuturistic imaginations, driven by both external techno-orientalist attributions and deeply internalized self-conceptualizations. Yet, these technological promises frequently present a paradox: they commodify the future while masking persistent social and structural inequalities in the present. Acknowledging that both area studies and science and technology studies (STS) discursively construct their respective subjects, this introduction bridges the two fields by charting the conceptual landscape of the ‘futuristic imagination sprawl’. It demonstrates that differentiating Sheila Jasanoff’s sociotechnical imaginaries from adjacent concepts enriches our investigation of future-oriented imaginations with greater clarity and precision. Grounded in this framework, the special issue’s case studies examine how Japanese technofutures are envisioned, institutionalized, translated, and contested from the 1960s to the present.

items.title: The HCI-H Model: Development of a Context-Sensitive Mathematical Framework for Prospective Healthcare Procedure Risk Assessment and Preventive Decision Support
items.abstract: This project proposes the development of the HCI-H Model, a multidimensional mathematical framework designed to assess the risk of harm associated with healthcare procedures according to local clinical and organizational conditions. The model integrates human factors, organizational risks, punitive culture, professional hierarchy, humanization of care, patient vulnerability, artificial intelligence-related risks, clinical decision-making, and the unjustified dismissal of safety warnings. Risk management and organizational resilience are incorporated as protective factors. The proposed mathematical equation aims to generate a relative risk score that may support the prospective identification of unsafe conditions and inform decisions regarding additional preventive measures, supervision, and safety barriers. This research protocol presents the theoretical foundations, mathematical formulation, and proposed methods for examining the model's consistency, sensitivity, and applicability across healthcare settings. The HCI-H Model is currently a theoretical framework under development. Its mathematical assumptions, predictive performance, and clinical utility require further empirical validation before implementation as a clinical decision-support tool.

items.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on clinical decision-making and patient safety: A narrative review
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), in the form of large language models (LLMs), has entered clinical practice faster than the evidence on how it changes clinical decisions could be produced. The relevant question is therefore no longer whether these models hold medical knowledge, but whether their use makes clinicians' decisions better and patients' care safer. This narrative review examines the evidence on the impact of generative AI on clinical decision-making and patient safety. In evaluations of encoded knowledge, a medically aligned model gave answers that agreed with scientific consensus in 92.6% of cases, against 92.9% for clinicians. In diagnostic reasoning, a model optimized for diagnosis outperformed unassisted clinicians on challenging cases and improved the differential diagnoses of the clinicians who used it, whereas a randomized trial of a general-purpose chatbot found no significant improvement in physicians' diagnostic reasoning, although the model alone outperformed both physician groups. In management reasoning, physicians assisted by GPT-4 scored 6.5 percentage points higher than those using conventional resources. When tested on real patient data in a simulated clinical workflow, however, LLMs diagnosed less accurately than physicians, did not follow guidelines and were sensitive to the order and quantity of information. The safety literature identifies four recurrent hazards: fabricated content, with hallucination rates of 50% to 82% when prompts contained a false clinical detail; misjudgement of clinical acuity, with drafted patient messages judged to pose a risk of severe harm in 7.1% of assessments; automation bias, by which clinicians adopt the model's assessment in place of their own; and the reproduction of racial and gender stereotypes. Only about 5% of published evaluations used real patient care data. Taken together, the evidence supports generative AI as a supervised aid to clinical reasoning rather than as an autonomous decision-maker, and indicates that its safety depends as much on the design of the human–AI interaction as on the accuracy of the model. Practical safeguards for clinical use are also reviewed.
